clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton began drinking at lunch with a warning at work; his wife Celeste left him by August; your mother's anxiety rose as she lay awake over them; your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. By May 1979, your grandmother took a job at the library and her functioning came back; these shifts in those months belong together as the family's reactions to the loss.

clusters.name: Odette's bedrest in pregnancy, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bedrest ordered for the rest of her pregnancy in March 1984, within months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it. These shifts cluster around your mother's drop in functioning and settle with your sister Ines's birth in September; they belong together as your household's reaction to her illness in pregnancy.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the next decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and care and overfunctioned; your father phoned his father every night for news and his anxiety rose; he and your uncle Lyle argued over who should help their parents; your grandfather's chest pains began; your father drank most evenings; by early 1996 your grandfather gave up his workshop and hardly left her side, his functioning down; your father fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. The shifts build slowly over years with only partial relief between them, each step widening the pull on your father's household, until your grandmother moved to the nursing home in June 1997 and the troubles settled.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum's departure to the mines in May 1999, within months: he and your father argued most nights over his plans to go north; your mother's anxiety rose as she could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage, his functioning down; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn, her functioning down; your mother took Ines with her everywhere and held her close; by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams, her functioning up, and the period settles.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May, your functioning down; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark, your anxiety up.
